test.name: A precise source refining a vague conclusion is an improvement, not a contradiction
test.description: Check 2's first gap. The profile records a birth of '1814' in 'Ireland'; the attached Catholic parish baptism (SD-DRIS-A) states 12 March 1814 at Skibbereen, Co. Cork. Nothing here disagrees -- the precise date falls inside the vague year and the precise parish inside the vague country -- so the source refines the conclusion rather than contradicting it, and reporting it as a finding is noise in a list the skill exists to triage. The shipped body covers numeric drift by record type ('a census age or birth year within a couple of years ... is ordinary variance') but says nothing about a difference in PRECISION rather than in value, so it has no rule that separates this from a conflict. The edit supplies one, and makes it checkable rather than a matter of taste: the test is containment, so '1814' against '12 March 1814' is a refinement while '1814' against '12 March 1815' is a finding. This corpus deliberately also carries a genuine index error (SD-DRIS-B) so that a run which correctly reports no finding for the baptism still has something for the Remediation doctrine, Classification and Signal-versus-noise dimensions to grade -- all three have N/A clauses that would otherwise score null, which is both a weaker test and the shape the review sample's targeted slot pulls in. PRE-EDIT BASELINE: not yet measured; step 0a of the plan records it here.

input.user_message: Audit the sources on Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) and list what is actually wrong with them, worst first.

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions to enumerate what is attached, then record_read each source that carries a record ARK

The profile's birth is '1814' / 'Ireland'. The baptism record (SD-DRIS-A) gives '12 March 1814' / 'Skibbereen, Cork, Ireland'. Grade whether the reply distinguishes a difference in precision from a difference in value: the record's date and place are narrower than the profile's and fall inside them, and no value in either contradicts the other.

Presenting that pair among the things wrong with the profile's sources is over-reporting of the kind this skill's own body warns about -- 'a list padded with non-findings is the same failure as a list padded with backend metadata'. Offering the fuller date and parish as an improvement the researcher could adopt is not a finding and should not be penalised as one.

The record also names a father Timothy and a mother Mary who are on no tool response for the profile. That is a completeness gap in the tree, not a defect in the source, and is outside what this skill audits.

The Drouin Collection marriage register (SD-DRIS-B) indexes 9 June 1845 against the profile's 9 June 1849 -- same day, same month, same bride, same parish. A marriage register states its date rather than estimating an age, so this is the corpus's genuine index error and the remedy is to go back to the original page and correct the index. The collection is 'database with images', so an image does exist here -- unlike an index-only collection, where there is nothing to re-read.

The 1861 census indexes a birth of 1816, two years off the baptism's 1814. Census ages were estimated, so a two-year drift is ordinary variance and not a finding. Saying nothing about it is acceptable.

The findings count must exclude the baptism refinement and the census drift. Repeated internal ids across the record responses (P1, N1, F1, S1 recurring on unrelated records) are FamilySearch storage artifacts and must not appear as numbered findings or carry a recommended action.
The headstone photograph (SD-DRIS-F) has no record ARK and must be reported as unchecked rather than clean
